title: Predicting ZIP Level Housing Values in Los Angeles County: A Machine Learning Approach Using Public Data
content: This study develops a machine learning framework for predicting residential home values at the ZIP code level across Los Angeles County using exclusively public data sources. Four datasets are integrated: the Zillow Home Value Index (ZHVI) for single family residences, LA County Assessor parcel records covering 12 million properties, the US Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) median household income estimates for 2011 through 2024, and the Redfin ZIP Code Market Tracker providing transaction level signals by ZIP code. Seven model families are evaluated across two experimental settings: a cross sectional data set of 267 ZIP codes and a panel data set of approximately 3,700 ZIP year observations covering 2011 to 2024. In the cross sectional setting, Random Forest achieves RMSE of $97,371 and R2 of 0.937. In the panel setting, a strict temporal split trains on pre COVID data (2011 to 2020) and tests on the post COVID period (2021 to 2024), where Gradient Boosting achieves RMSE of $166,041 and R2 of 0.950. A one year forecast extension using lagged price and momentum features achieves R2 0.992 and RMSE of $62,502. Tree based ensembles consistently outperform linear models across every setting, with linear models showing near complete failure in the panel context. ZIP level Redfin market signals, particularly median price per square foot, emerge as the single most informative feature in the panel model, contributing 41.6% of the Gradient Boosting model’s total feature importance.
